explanations.explanation: Moses says it plainly: arm some men "that they may go against the Midianites and execute the LORD’s vengeance on them." (Numbers 31:3) The vengeance isn't Moses' idea. It comes from what the LORD told him in verse 2. So the army goes out as the ones carrying out the LORD's word, and that's the whole point.

I can see why you'd pick Moses, since he's the one giving the orders. But listen to how he says it: "execute the LORD’s vengeance on them." (Numbers 31:3) He's passing along what the LORD said to him in verse 2. Moses is the messenger here, friend, not the owner.

The army is the one marching, so that guess makes sense. But Moses doesn't call it theirs. He says they are to "execute the LORD’s vengeance on them." (Numbers 31:3) The men go because the LORD commanded it, not because they had a score of their own to settle.

True! The text says they "waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 31:7) Nobody is freelancing here. The order came from the LORD, and the army carried it out the way it was given.
Not quite, friend. Verse 7 says they "waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 31:7) So the army did what it was told. The answer is True.

explanations.answer: Their herds and flocks and goods
explanations.explanation: Yes! Verse 9 says they "plundered all their herds, flocks, and goods." (Numbers 31:9) The women and children were captured, and the animals and belongings were taken too. It was a big haul, and the numbers later in the chapter show just how big.

Idols and altars are a fair guess, but they don't show up in this verse. The text says the Israelites "plundered all their herds, flocks, and goods." (Numbers 31:9) So the plunder was animals and belongings. I'd keep my eyes on the actual list the verse gives.

Wells and fields would be hard to carry home, friend. I can barely carry two cookie sheets and a mixing bowl at once. The verse says they "plundered all their herds, flocks, and goods." (Numbers 31:9) That means animals and things they could take with them.

Right, "burn." The text says they "burned all the cities where the Midianites had lived, as well as all their encampments." (Numbers 31:10) Both the cities and the encampments went up. It's a heavy detail, and the text gives it straight.

Rebuilding is a kind thought, but that's not what happened. Verse 10 says they "burned all the cities where the Midianites had lived, as well as all their encampments." (Numbers 31:10) The cities and encampments were burned. The word that fits the blank is "burn."

Moving in is a natural guess, since people usually settle where they win. But the verse says they "burned all the cities where the Midianites had lived, as well as all their encampments." (Numbers 31:10) Nothing there about moving in. It says they burned them.

Not this time, friend. The text says they "carried away all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals." (Numbers 31:11) Then they brought "the captives, spoils, and plunder" to Moses. (Numbers 31:12) So the plunder came back too, and the answer is False.

False is right! The army carried away "all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals." (Numbers 31:11) And they brought "the captives, spoils, and plunder" to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the congregation. (Numbers 31:12) Nothing got left behind on the road.

explanations.answer: If they spared all the women
explanations.explanation: That's the one! Moses asks the officers, "Have you spared all the women?" (Numbers 31:15) He's angry when he asks it, and the very next verse is where he explains himself. I think those officers got real quiet, real fast.

explanations.answer: Why they killed the five kings
explanations.explanation: Close, because the kings were mentioned earlier. But Moses never asks about them. His question is, "Have you spared all the women?" (Numbers 31:15) His anger is about the women, and that's where the rest of his words go.

explanations.answer: Where Phinehas had gone off to
explanations.explanation: Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, did go with the army, so I see the thought. But Moses never asks where he is. He asks, "Have you spared all the women?" (Numbers 31:15) That's the question that comes out of his anger.

Yes, Balaam son of Beor! Moses says the women caused Israel to turn unfaithfully "through the counsel of Balaam." (Numbers 31:16) Balaam was already named among the slain in verse 8. Here Moses ties his name to what happened at Peor.

Balak, king of Moab, is a name from Balaam's story, so I get why it came to mind. But Moses doesn't name him here. He says it was "through the counsel of Balaam." (Numbers 31:16) That's Balaam son of Beor.

Og, king of Bashan, is a king Israel met on the road, but he isn't in this verse. Moses says the women caused it "through the counsel of Balaam." (Numbers 31:16) So the answer is Balaam son of Beor. Og can sit this one out.

Right, the "congregation." The LORD says to "divide the captives between the troops who went out to battle and the rest of the congregation." (Numbers 31:27) Two shares, one for the soldiers and one for everybody else. Splitting it fairly is how you keep the whole camp happy.

Elders is a reasonable guess, since leaders are all over this chapter. But the LORD says the captives are divided between the troops "and the rest of the congregation." (Numbers 31:27) The second half goes to the whole congregation, not just the elders.

The commanders are in this chapter, so that's a fair pick. But the verse says to divide the captives between the troops "and the rest of the congregation." (Numbers 31:27) The commanders were already part of the army. The other half goes to the congregation.

Not quite, friend. The commanders say, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one of us is missing." (Numbers 31:49) Nobody was missing, so the answer is False. Every man made it back.
False is right! The commanders say, "not one of us is missing." (Numbers 31:49) They counted every soldier under their command, and everyone was there. I'd have counted twice and still been nervous.

That's it! The commanders say they brought the gold offering "to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD." (Numbers 31:50) They gave armlets, bracelets, rings, earrings and necklaces. The text states the reason in their own words.

explanations.answer: To pay for the army's weapons
explanations.explanation: Paying for weapons sounds practical, but the commanders never say that. They bring the gold "to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD." (Numbers 31:50) So the offering is about atonement, not about covering costs.

explanations.answer: To thank Moses for leading them
explanations.explanation: Thanking Moses would be a nice gesture, but that isn't what they say. The offering goes to the LORD, and they bring it "to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD." (Numbers 31:50) The gold is for atonement, friend.

True! Verse 53 says it simply: "Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself." (Numbers 31:53) It's a short line, but it tells you the soldiers kept something of their own. I think it's worth a pause that it sits right after all that gold for the LORD.
Not this time, friend. The text says, "Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself." (Numbers 31:53) Every soldier took some, so the answer is True.

Yes! Moses and Eleazar brought the gold "into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD." (Numbers 31:54) The gold didn't get stashed in someone's tent. It went to the Tent of Meeting, where it stood as a memorial.

explanations.answer: Up to the top of Mount Nebo
explanations.explanation: Mount Nebo is a mountain Moses climbs later in his story, so I see where that came from. But in this verse, they brought the gold "into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD." (Numbers 31:54) No mountain climbing needed. The Tent of Meeting was right there in the camp.

explanations.answer: Across to the city of Jericho
explanations.explanation: Jericho was close by, just across the Jordan from the camp, so the guess makes sense. But Jericho isn't where the gold went. Verse 54 says they brought it "into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD." (Numbers 31:54)
